title.value: Predicting Tactical Solutions to Operational Planning Problems under Imperfect Information
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the paper's metadata and introduction section.
title.quote: This paper offers a methodological contribution at the intersection of machine learning and operations research. Namely, we propose a method- ology to quickly predict expected tactical descriptions of operational solu- tions (TDOSs).

extractions.description: This paper proposes a methodology that integrates machine learning and operations research to predict tactical descriptions of operational solutions quickly. The approach focuses on improving computational speed and accuracy in predicting solutions to complex problems under imperfect information conditions. The methodology utilizes a supervised learning model trained on deterministic operational problems to predict solutions in a two-stage stochastic programming context. The paper emphasizes applications in railway container booking and load planning.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily discusses methodologies in machine learning and operations research, with specific application examples in tactical and operational planning, without any direct focus on climate change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Keywords: supervised learning, deep learning, integer linear programming, stochastic programming

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address any of the predefined climate change categories or sub-categories. It focuses on machine learning methodologies applied to operations research domains like railway planning, not specifically climate-related systems.
primary_category.quote: The problem we address occurs in the context of two-stage stochastic programming where the second stage is demanding computationally. We aim to predict at a high speed the expected TDOS associated with the second stage problem, conditionally on the first stage variables.

primary_sub_category.justification: The application's scope and machine learning methodology described in the paper do not align with any specific climate change sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: As a motivating application, we consider a myopic, two-stage booking con- trol problem pertaining to cargo capacity management.

applications.value: Railway container booking and load planning optimization
applications.justification: The methodology is applied to predicting tactical solutions within the context of railway container booking as a motivating example of the approach.
applications.quote: To illustrate the methodology, we specialize the two-stage booking prob- lem to reflect the booking decisions made about the shipment of intermodal containers by rail at our industrial partner.
